New guard at attest.py:587: `elif _authoritative_material(attestation) is None:` makes the whole-HEAD check conditional on NO bound material, contradicting the unconditional 'when unscoped, whole-HEAD freshness' phrasing in the docstring.
advisory.finding: The `compute_validity` docstring still describes the old unscoped behavior ('when unscoped, whole-HEAD freshness; plus material-fingerprint invariance'), but after this change whole-HEAD freshness is only a fail-closed fallback for material-LESS unscoped records; the normal (material-bound) unscoped case is anchored on material-fingerprint invariance alone.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword the plan-review bullet to: 'scoped code-drift ...; when unscoped and a material fingerprint is bound, freshness is anchored on material-fingerprint invariance; only material-LESS unscoped records fall back to whole-HEAD freshness.'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm it is acceptable that unscoped material-bound plan-review attestations no longer invalidate on real code drift (material fingerprint excludes code contents), since the whole-HEAD catch-all is now bypassed for them.
evidence: pass1.py:551-562: `material_fingerprint` basis = ticket_id/description/file_impact/children only — code file contents are NOT included.

attest.py:597-600 comment: 'an unscoped plan's freshness is anchored on its material fingerprint, so unrelated head drift no longer forces stale-head' — but material fingerprint does not cover code, so RELATED code drift is also no longer caught for unscoped plans.
Commit message acknowledges the residual is out of scope: 'Scope: this fixes the deterministic trigger only ... tracked as follow-up 0916-8c47-6205-4a37.'
advisory.finding: For an unscoped, material-bound plan-review attestation, the material fingerprint hashes only ticket plan content (description/file_impact/children), not code file contents, so genuine CODE drift no longer invalidates the attestation — where the previous whole-HEAD check would have caught it via stale-head. This relaxes drift detection for all unscoped material-bound plans, not just those hit by unrelated commits.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: unscoped attestation with a bound `material:` line and `_fp(monkeypatch, None)` (current fingerprint uncomputable) asserts verdict == 'unverifiable-material' and valid is False.
evidence: Before the fix an unscoped material-bound record hit the head check first (returning stale-head on drift); after the `elif ... is None` guard it falls through to line 613, so the `unverifiable-material` branch is now reachable for unscoped+material-bound records.

ABSENCE: the three new tests cover material-unchanged (test_plan_review_unscoped_unrelated_head_drift_stays_valid), material-changed (test_plan_review_unscoped_material_change_still_invalidates), and material-less (test_plan_review_unscoped_head_drift_stale_when_no_material_bound), but none set `_fp(monkeypatch, None)` WITH a bound `material:` line to reach unverifiable-material.
advisory.finding: The fix newly routes an unscoped, material-BOUND attestation past the whole-HEAD check into the material-invariance block, making the `unverifiable-material` verdict (attest.py:619-624) newly reachable for this record class when `current_material_fingerprint` returns None. No test exercises this fail-closed path; a regression that certified (rather than rejected) an unscoped record whose material fingerprint cannot be recomputed would go undetected.
scenarios: Unscoped plan-review attestation with a bound material fingerprint whose current fingerprint recompute fails (returns None) — must fail closed as unverifiable-material, not certify.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_plan_review_unscoped_material_change_still_invalidates but with `_fp(monkeypatch, None)` and a manifest carrying `material: pm`, asserting `res["valid"] is False and res["verdict"] == "unverifiable-material"`.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that dropping the whole-HEAD code-drift proxy for material-bound UNSCOPED plan-review attestations is intended, given the material fingerprint covers only plan text (not code) and no per-file dep map exists to catch code drift.
evidence: attest.py:587 `elif _authoritative_material(attestation) is None:` — the whole-HEAD fallback now runs ONLY for material-less records
attest.py:567-569 comment: `Code-drift freshness (ADR 0002): ... when unscoped, fall back to conservative whole-HEAD freshness.` — the whole-HEAD check WAS the unscoped code-drift guard
pass1.py:551-562 `material_fingerprint`: basis = {ticket_id, description, file_impact, children} — plan text only, no code content; so material invariance does not detect code drift
attest.py:570-576: the per-path `deps` re-hash (`stale-code`) only runs when `deps` is non-empty (scoped); an unscoped plan skips it entirely

Combined reachability: unscoped + material-bound attestation + code drift (HEAD advances with real code changes) → neither stale-code, stale-material, nor stale-head fires → verdict stays `certified` (attest.py:634-638)
blocking.finding: The change removes the only code-drift freshness guard for material-bound UNSCOPED plan-review attestations. An unscoped plan has no per-file dep-hash map (the `stale-code` check does not run), and the bound material fingerprint hashes ONLY plan text (description/file_impact/children — pass1.py:551-562), NOT repository code. Previously the whole-HEAD SHA check invalidated (`stale-head`) on any HEAD advance, serving as the conservative code-drift proxy for unscoped plans; now it fires only when NO material fingerprint is bound. Result: a material-bound unscoped plan-review attestation stays `certified` while the code it was reviewed against drifts arbitrarily, causing the claim gate to short-circuit re-review of changed code.
scenarios: An unscoped plan-review is certified at HEAD=A; a later commit changes source files the plan depends on but not the ticket text; the claim gate reads the attestation as `certified` and skips re-review of the drifted code.
